question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Abide
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dwell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abide" (verb) means to stay, remain or live in a place; to continue/endure. Its closest synonym here is "dwell", which also means to live or reside in a place. (निवास करना / ठहरना)

◦ Example: He abided/dwelt in that little hill town for many years.

• Both words also share the sense of "to remain for a long time" — "the memory abides" / "let us not dwell on the past".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Repudiate" means to reject or refuse to accept (अस्वीकार करना) — the opposite idea.

• Option 2 "Decamp" means to leave suddenly and secretly (चुपके से भाग जाना) — an antonym of abide/stay.

• Option 4 "Vamoose" is informal for to depart quickly, to run off (भाग जाना) — again the opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of abide: dwell, reside, stay, remain, tolerate, bear. Antonyms: depart, leave, decamp, vamoose.

• Remember the common usage "abide by" = to obey/comply with (abide by the rules).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To pull the trigger
option_3: To insult and disgrace the people
option_4: To commit a course of action
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To commit a course of action.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to pull the trigger" means to take the decisive step; to finally commit oneself to a course of action after thinking about it. (निर्णायक कदम उठाना / अंतिम निर्णय ले लेना)

◦ Example: After months of hesitation, the company finally pulled the trigger on the merger.

• The image comes from firing a gun — once the trigger is pulled, the action cannot be undone; hence it means committing irrevocably to a decision.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To make an exaggerated statement" would be the idiom "to draw the long bow" or "to blow things out of proportion".

• Option 2 "To do unnecessary things" is closer to "to carry coals to Newcastle" / "to gild the lily".

• Option 3 "To insult and disgrace the people" would suit "to drag someone through the mud".

NOTE

• Related decision-making idioms: "take the plunge" (to do something risky at last), "bite the bullet" (to endure something unpleasant bravely), "cross the Rubicon" (to pass the point of no return).

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ornage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ornage" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Orange" — the fruit/colour. (संतरा / नारंगी)

• Spelling key: O + RANGE → ORANGE. The learner's error here is the transposition of "a" and "n" (Orn-age instead of Or-ange).

◦ Correct: She peeled an orange and shared it with her friend.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Famous" (well known, celebrated — प्रसिद्ध), "Leader" (one who leads — नेता) and "Flowing" (moving smoothly like a liquid — बहता हुआ) are all correctly spelt.

• Note that "famous" ends in -ous (not -ious): famous, nervous, jealous, dangerous.

NOTE

• Watch out for other commonly transposed spellings in SSC exams: receive (not recieve), separate (not seperate), definitely (not definately), maintenance (not maintainance).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Raccoons have being more active at night.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. are more.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "have being" is not a valid verb form in English at all — "being" is the present participle of "be" and can never follow "have" in this structure (we may say "have been", never "have being").

• The sentence states a general/habitual fact about raccoons, so the simple present is required: "Raccoons are more active at night."

◦ Correct: Raccoons are more active at night.

• "more active" is the correct comparative of the long adjective "active" (more active / most active), which fits the implied comparison with daytime.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "are few" is wrong — "few" is used with countable plural nouns (few raccoons), not with an adjective like "active".

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "have being" is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 "are much" is wrong — "much" cannot directly qualify the adjective "active" here; we would need "much more active".

NOTE

• Universal truths and habitual facts take the simple present tense: "The sun rises in the east", "Owls hunt at night", "Raccoons are more active at night".

• Distinguish been (past participle of be — used after have/has/had) from being (present participle — used after am/is/are/was/were).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Professor Murli's eyebrows / rose a little higher and his / gaze became distinctly coldest.
option_4: rose a little higher and his
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. gaze became distinctly coldest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The superlative degree ("coldest") is used when three or more things are compared, or with "the". Here only a change of degree in one person's gaze is described, and the parallel clause already uses the comparative "higher"; hence the comparative "colder" is required.

◦ Correct: Professor Murli's eyebrows rose a little higher and his gaze became distinctly colder.

• A superlative also normally needs the article "the" ("the coldest gaze in the room"), which is missing here — another sign that "coldest" is wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 3 "Professor Murli's eyebrows" is correct — the possessive of a singular noun is formed with 's.

• Segment 4 "rose a little higher and his" is correct — "rose" is the correct past tense of the intransitive verb "rise" (rise – rose – risen), and "higher" is a properly formed comparative.

• Hence "No error" (Option 2) cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: cold – colder – coldest, high – higher – highest. Use the comparative for two things/states and the superlative (with "the") for three or more.

• Do not confuse rise (intransitive: rise, rose, risen — no object) with raise (transitive: raise, raised, raised — takes an object).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Reverence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Scorn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reverence" means deep respect, awe and admiration for someone or something. (श्रद्धा / गहरा सम्मान)

• Its antonym is "Scorn", which means contempt, disdain, a feeling that someone is worthless. (तिरस्कार / अवमानना)

◦ Example: The pilgrims looked at the shrine with reverence, but the cynic looked at it with scorn.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Venerate" means to regard with great respect — a synonym in idea (though a verb), not an antonym.

• Option 2 "Honour" means high respect/esteem — again a synonym of reverence.

• Option 4 "Deference" means humble submission and respect — also a synonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of reverence: veneration, awe, homage, deference, honour, adoration.

• Antonyms of reverence: scorn, contempt, disdain, derision, disrespect, irreverence.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

On the job
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Working at a particular job.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "on the job" means engaged in / while doing one's work; actually working at a particular job. (काम पर / काम करते हुए)

◦ Example: He learnt most of his skills on the job rather than in a classroom.

• The very common collocation "on-the-job training" means training given while a person is actually performing the work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "In the war" corresponds to phrases like "on the front" / "in the field", not "on the job".

• Option 2 "Avoiding the work" is the meaning of "to shirk", "to goldbrick" or "to dodge work" — the opposite of being on the job.

• Option 4 "On the contrary" is an entirely different discourse marker used to contradict a previous statement.

NOTE

• Related work idioms: "burn the midnight oil" (work late into the night), "put one's shoulder to the wheel" (work hard), "call it a day" (stop working for the day).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Without the greenhouse effect, Earths temperature would be below freezing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Earths temperature would.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Earths" is missing the apostrophe of possession. Since the temperature belongs to the Earth, the possessive form "Earth's" is required.

◦ Correct: Without the greenhouse effect, Earth's temperature would be below freezing.

• Rule: a singular noun forms the possessive by adding apostrophe + s ('s) — the Earth's crust, the boy's book, India's economy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "Without the greenhouse effect," is correct — a proper prepositional phrase used to express a condition.

• Segment "be below freezing." is correct — "would be" is the right conditional form matching the implied "if" idea in "Without ...".

• Hence "No error" (Option 4) cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• "Earths" without an apostrophe would be a plural noun (many earths), which is not intended here.

• Do not confuse its (possessive — "its temperature") with it's (it is). The apostrophe rule for possession applies to nouns, not to possessive pronouns.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

With a (sudden push off understanding), Harry realised who the people in the end beds must be.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. sudden rush of understanding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The natural English collocation for a sudden realisation is "a sudden rush of understanding" — "rush" here means a sudden strong surge of feeling or comprehension. (समझ का अचानक उमड़ना)

◦ Correct: With a sudden rush of understanding, Harry realised who the people in the end beds must be.

• The bracketed phrase "sudden push off understanding" is wrong on two counts: "push" does not collocate with understanding, and "off" should be the preposition "of".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "suddenly rushed understanding" is grammatically wrong — after the article "a" and the preposition "With", a noun phrase is required, not an adverb + past participle.

• Option 3 "No correction required" is wrong because the given phrase is both idiomatically and grammatically faulty.

• Option 4 "all of sudden understand" is wrong — the idiom is "all of a sudden" (with the article "a"), and a verb cannot follow "With a".

NOTE

• Similar collocations: "a rush of blood", "a rush of emotion", "a flash of insight", "a wave of relief", "a pang of guilt".

• Beware of the common confusion between of (belonging to) and off (away from).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The most common sports injury is a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. bruise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "bruise" is an injury in which the skin is not broken but a dark mark appears because of bleeding underneath — the commonest kind of sports injury. (चोट का नील / खरोंच)

◦ Correct: The most common sports injury is a bruise.

• The blank follows the article "a" and needs a countable noun naming an injury — only "bruise" fits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "brush" is an implement for cleaning/painting (or a brief encounter, "a brush with the law") — not an injury.

• Option 3 "brews" is a plural noun/verb form relating to making tea, coffee or beer — it also cannot follow the singular article "a".

• Option 4 "breve" is a musical note (a double whole note) or a diacritical mark — unrelated.

NOTE

• Common sports-injury vocabulary: bruise (contusion), sprain (stretched/torn ligament), strain (pulled muscle), fracture (broken bone), dislocation, cramp.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

You should never judge a person without knowing the truth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. decide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Judge" (verb) means to form an opinion about, to assess or decide about someone or something. Its closest synonym among the options is "decide". (निर्णय करना / राय बनाना)

◦ Example: Do not judge/decide about a person's character on first impressions alone.

• Both words share the core sense of arriving at a conclusion or verdict after considering evidence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "wink" means to close and open one eye quickly as a signal (आँख मारना) — unrelated.

• Option 3 "pacify" means to calm someone down, to bring peace (शांत करना) — unrelated.

• Option 4 "care" means to feel concern or look after (परवाह करना) — unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of judge (verb): decide, assess, evaluate, appraise, adjudge, deem, consider.

• As a noun, a judge is an official who decides cases in a court of law; related words: judgement, judicial, judiciary, judicious (showing good sense).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A residence for nuns
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Convent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "convent" is a building or community in which nuns live, dedicated to religious life. (मठ — जहाँ नन/भिक्षुणियाँ रहती हैं)

◦ Example: She spent twenty years teaching in a convent school run by nuns.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Refugee" is a person forced to flee his or her country — a person, not a residence.

• Option 3 "Monastery" is a residence for monks (not nuns) — the standard SSC contrast with "convent".

• Option 4 "Mint" is a place where coins/currency are manufactured (टकसाल), or an aromatic herb.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes frequently asked in SSC exams: Monastery (monks), Convent/Nunnery (nuns), Hermitage (a hermit), Presbytery (a priest), Sanatorium (patients recovering), Orphanage (orphans), Aviary (birds), Apiary (bees).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

All work and none play makes Jack a dull boy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. no play.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard proverb is "All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy", meaning a person who only works and never relaxes becomes boring/dull. (केवल काम और मनोरंजन बिल्कुल नहीं — व्यक्ति नीरस हो जाता है)

• Grammatically, the determiner "no" must be used directly before a noun ("no play"), whereas "none" is a pronoun that stands alone and cannot be placed before a noun.

◦ Correct: All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong — "none play" is ungrammatical.

• Option 3 "none plays" wrongly turns "play" into a verb and breaks the parallel with the noun "work".

• Option 4 "no played" wrongly uses a past-participle/past form after the determiner "no".

NOTE

• no + noun (no play, no money, no time) vs none of + noun / none alone (none of the boys, none came).

• The parallel structure "All work and no play" requires two nouns joined by "and"; the singular verb "makes" agrees with the whole idea treated as one unit.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Since the temperatures can soar in summer, choose clothing that is lightweight and ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. breathable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Breathable" describes fabric that allows air and moisture to pass through, keeping the wearer cool — exactly what is needed when "temperatures can soar in summer". (हवादार कपड़ा)

◦ Correct: Since the temperatures can soar in summer, choose clothing that is lightweight and breathable.

• The word must also be parallel in sense with "lightweight", i.e. another comfort-in-heat quality; only "breathable" qualifies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "airtight" means sealed so that no air can pass — it would trap heat and sweat, the opposite of what summer clothing needs.

• Option 3 "bulky" means large and heavy — it contradicts "lightweight".

• Option 4 "hefty" means heavy and substantial — again contradicts "lightweight".

NOTE

• "Soar" here means to rise very high/rapidly (तेज़ी से बढ़ना). Do not confuse it with "sore" (painful).

• Breathable fabrics for summer: cotton, linen, khadi, muslin — they permit ventilation and quick evaporation of sweat.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

______ every nation in the world is now administering vaccines.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Nearly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adverb of degree meaning "almost" to modify the quantifier phrase "every nation". That adverb is "Nearly". (लगभग)

◦ Correct: Nearly every nation in the world is now administering vaccines.

• "Nearly/almost + every/all/half" is a standard English pattern: "nearly every student", "almost all the books".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Near" is a preposition/adjective of place ("near the school", "the near future") and cannot modify "every nation" in this sense.

• Option 3 "Nearest" is the superlative of near ("the nearest hospital") — a degree of distance, not of quantity.

• Option 4 "Nearer" is the comparative of near ("come nearer") — again about distance.

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb: near (adjective/preposition — distance) vs nearly (adverb — almost, degree). Compare: "He lives near the park" / "He nearly fell down".

• Synonyms of nearly: almost, virtually, practically, all but.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

My research focus on marine mammal behaviour, ecology and conservation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. My research focus on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "My research" is a singular uncountable noun, so the verb must take the singular "-s" form: "focuses", not "focus".

◦ Correct: My research focuses on marine mammal behaviour, ecology and conservation.

• This is a classic subject–verb agreement error: singular subject → singular verb (he focuses, my research focuses); plural subject → plural verb (they focus, my studies focus).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment "marine mammal behaviour," is correct — a properly formed noun phrase with the British spelling "behaviour".

• Segment "ecology and conservation." is correct — the three items after "on" (behaviour, ecology, conservation) are properly parallel nouns.

• Hence "No error" (Option 3) cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• "Research", "information", "advice", "furniture", "equipment", "news" and "luggage" are uncountable and always take a singular verb.

• The verb "focus" takes the preposition "on" — "focus on the target".

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

It was a very generous and jolly voice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. morose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jolly" means cheerful, merry and full of good humour. (प्रसन्नचित्त / खुशमिजाज़)

• Its antonym is "morose", meaning gloomy, sullen and bad-tempered. (उदास / खिन्न)

◦ Example: The jolly shopkeeper greeted everyone warmly, while his morose assistant never smiled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "tabular" means arranged in the form of a table (सारणीबद्ध) — unrelated to mood.

• Option 3 "festive" means cheerful and celebratory — a synonym of jolly, not an antonym.

• Option 4 "witty" means clever and amusing in speech — related to humour, hence closer to a synonym than an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of jolly: cheerful, merry, jovial, genial, jubilant, festive.

• Antonyms of jolly: morose, gloomy, sullen, melancholy, dour, glum.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

One who has lost one's parents
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Orphan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "orphan" is a child whose parents are dead, i.e., one who has lost one's parents. (अनाथ)

◦ Example: After the accident, the little boy was left an orphan and was raised by his aunt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Recluse" is a person who lives alone and avoids other people (एकांतवासी).

• Option 2 "Martyr" is a person who dies for a cause or belief (शहीद).

• Option 4 "Snob" is a person who looks down on those of lower social status (दंभी व्यक्ति).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Widow (a woman whose husband is dead), Widower (a man whose wife is dead), Orphanage (a home for orphans), Bachelor (an unmarried man), Spinster (an unmarried woman).

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: It is not even a consciuos process.
option_2: It is not even a concious process.
option_3: It is not even a conscious proccess.
option_4: It is not even a conscious process.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. It is not even a conscious process.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The two key words must be spelt "conscious" (aware, deliberate — सचेत) and "process" (a series of steps — प्रक्रिया).

• Spelling key: CON + SCI + OUS → CONSCIOUS; PRO + CESS (double s, single c) → PROCESS.

◦ Correct: It is not even a conscious process.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "consciuos" wrongly reverses "io" to "uo".

• Option 2 "concious" drops the "s" of the "-sci-" cluster.

• Option 3 "proccess" wrongly doubles the "c".

NOTE

• Word family: conscious (aware), consciously (adverb), consciousness (noun), subconscious, unconscious.

• Do not confuse conscious (aware) with conscience (the inner sense of right and wrong) or conscientious (careful and diligent).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

I am not sure ______ wearing this black dress.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. about.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "sure" takes the preposition "about" (or "of") when we express doubt regarding something: "sure about something". A gerund ("wearing") naturally follows the preposition.

◦ Correct: I am not sure about wearing this black dress.

• Rule: a preposition is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), never by an infinitive — "about wearing", "of going", "in doing".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "with" — "sure with" is not a valid collocation.

• Option 2 "in" — "sure in" is not standard English.

• Option 4 "off" — "sure off" is meaningless; note that "off" indicates separation/removal.

NOTE

• Common adjective + preposition collocations for SSC: sure/certain of/about, afraid of, fond of, good at, interested in, proud of, jealous of, angry with (a person) / at (a thing), married to, similar to.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

(1) ________ people think that we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country (2) ________ by living in that country. However, this is not necessarily true. Often, the longer we stay in a (3) ________ country, the more we realize how little we actually know about the culture of that country. Books and talks about other people's (4) ________ can even be dangerous because they concentrate on cultural differences and (5) ________ national character, and sometimes a lot of information they contain is untrue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Many.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by the plural countable noun "people" and the plural verb "think", so the quantifier must be a plural one — "Many people think ...". (बहुत से लोग)

• The passage then contradicts this common belief ("However, this is not necessarily true"), which shows that a widely held view is being reported — "Many people think" is exactly the standard way to introduce such a belief.

◦ Correct: Many people think that we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Few" would mean "hardly any", which destroys the logic — the writer is refuting a popular, not a rare, belief.

• Option 3 "Every" and Option 4 "Each" are singular determiners and would require a singular verb ("Every person thinks"), so they cannot go with "people think".

NOTE

• Quantifier–verb agreement: many/several/a few + plural noun + plural verb; each/every/either/neither + singular noun + singular verb.

• "Few" = hardly any (negative), "a few" = some (positive), "the few" = the small number there are.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

(1) ________ people think that we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country (2) ________ by living in that country. However, this is not necessarily true. Often, the longer we stay in a (3) ________ country, the more we realize how little we actually know about the culture of that country. Books and talks about other people's (4) ________ can even be dangerous because they concentrate on cultural differences and (5) ________ national character, and sometimes a lot of information they contain is untrue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. simply.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The belief being reported is that culture can be learnt "simply by living" in a country — i.e., merely/just by living there, with no other effort. (केवल / मात्र)

◦ Correct: ... we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country simply by living in that country.

• "Simply by + V-ing" is a fixed and very common English pattern meaning "just by doing something".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "precisely" means exactly/accurately — it does not convey the "merely" sense the sentence needs.

• Option 2 "directly" means without anything in between; it does not fit the idea of effortlessness that the writer goes on to challenge.

• Option 3 "formally" means officially/in a formal manner — the opposite of the informal, incidental learning implied here.

NOTE

• "Simply" has two senses: (i) merely/only ("simply by living") and (ii) in a plain manner ("she dressed simply"). Here sense (i) applies.

• Synonyms in this sense: merely, just, only, purely.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

(1) ________ people think that we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country (2) ________ by living in that country. However, this is not necessarily true. Often, the longer we stay in a (3) ________ country, the more we realize how little we actually know about the culture of that country. Books and talks about other people's (4) ________ can even be dangerous because they concentrate on cultural differences and (5) ________ national character, and sometimes a lot of information they contain is untrue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. foreign.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The whole passage is about learning the culture of a foreign country, and the first sentence already uses that exact phrase. The blank simply repeats the key idea: "the longer we stay in a foreign country". (विदेशी)

◦ Correct: Often, the longer we stay in a foreign country, the more we realize how little we actually know about the culture of that country.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "benign" means kind and gentle, or (in medicine) non-cancerous — irrelevant here.

• Option 3 "sovereign" means possessing supreme power/independent — "a sovereign country" is a valid phrase but breaks the passage's logic, which is about foreignness, not sovereignty.

• Option 4 "reign" is a noun/verb meaning the period of rule of a monarch — it cannot function as an adjective before "country".

NOTE

• The structure "the + comparative ..., the + comparative ..." ("the longer we stay, the more we realize") shows that two things increase together — a very common SSC grammar point.

• Note the spelling family with the silent "g": foreign, sovereign, reign, feign, deign.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

(1) ________ people think that we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country (2) ________ by living in that country. However, this is not necessarily true. Often, the longer we stay in a (3) ________ country, the more we realize how little we actually know about the culture of that country. Books and talks about other people's (4) ________ can even be dangerous because they concentrate on cultural differences and (5) ________ national character, and sometimes a lot of information they contain is untrue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. culture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is consistently about culture — "the culture of a foreign country", "cultural differences". The blank refers to "Books and talks about other people's culture". (संस्कृति)

◦ Correct: Books and talks about other people's culture can even be dangerous because they concentrate on cultural differences ...

• The very next clause mentions "cultural differences", confirming that "culture" is the word deleted.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "conjecture" means a guess based on incomplete information (अनुमान) — it does not fit "books and talks about other people's ...".

• Option 2 "caricature" is an exaggerated, comic portrait (व्यंग्य-चित्र) — attractive as a distractor because of the "exaggerate" theme later, but the phrase needed here is "other people's culture".

• Option 3 "stature" means height or standing/reputation (कद / प्रतिष्ठा) — unrelated.

NOTE

• Contextual clue technique: when a word from the blank reappears in a nearby sentence in another form (culture → cultural), that word is almost always the answer.

• Word family: culture, cultural, culturally, multicultural, acculturation.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

(1) ________ people think that we can learn a lot about the culture of a foreign country (2) ________ by living in that country. However, this is not necessarily true. Often, the longer we stay in a (3) ________ country, the more we realize how little we actually know about the culture of that country. Books and talks about other people's (4) ________ can even be dangerous because they concentrate on cultural differences and (5) ________ national character, and sometimes a lot of information they contain is untrue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. exaggerate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause explains why such books and talks are dangerous: they "concentrate on cultural differences and exaggerate national character" — i.e., they overstate/blow up national traits, which is why "a lot of information they contain is untrue". (बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर बताना)

◦ Correct: ... they concentrate on cultural differences and exaggerate national character ...

• The blank sits in a parallel verb structure after "and", so a plain verb form matching "concentrate" is required — "exaggerate" fits both grammatically and logically.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "considerate" is an adjective (thoughtful of others), so it cannot be the second verb after "and".

• Option 3 "proliferate" means to increase rapidly in number (तेज़ी से बढ़ना) — it does not take an object like "national character" in this sense.

• Option 4 "concentrate" is already used just before the blank; repeating it would be redundant and would not explain the untruth mentioned at the end.

NOTE

• Synonyms of exaggerate: overstate, magnify, embellish, blow out of proportion. Antonyms: understate, downplay, minimise.

• Do not confuse considerate (thoughtful) with considerable (large in amount).

question: The constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1949.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949, and it came into force on 26 January 1950. (संविधान अंगीकरण — 26 नवंबर 1949)

• 26 November is therefore celebrated every year as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas), declared in 2015.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan; its first sitting was on 9 December 1946.

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was its permanent Chairman; Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee (set up on 29 August 1947).

• Framing the Constitution took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

NOTE

• 26 January 1950 was chosen as the date of commencement because the Congress had celebrated Purna Swaraj Day on 26 January 1930.

• The original Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.

question: 'Ace against Odds' is an autobiographical book by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sania Mirza.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ace against Odds" (2016) is the autobiography of the Indian tennis star Sania Mirza, co-written with her father Imran Mirza and journalist Shivani Gupta. (सानिया मिर्ज़ा की आत्मकथा)

• The title plays on the tennis term "ace" — a serve the opponent cannot touch.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sania Mirza became World No. 1 in women's doubles and won six Grand Slam titles (three in women's doubles and three in mixed doubles).

• Her awards include the Arjuna Award (2004), Padma Shri (2006), Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2015) and Padma Bhushan (2016).

NOTE

• Other sports autobiographies: Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), Unbreakable (Mary Kom), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh), Straight from the Heart (Kapil Dev), My Life My Mission was not sport — V. V. Giri wrote My Life and Times.

question: Who among the following was the first Indian musician to receive the Grammy Life Time Achievement Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ravi Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar was the first Indian musician to receive the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award (2013), awarded posthumously. (पंडित रवि शंकर — सितार वादक)

• He is credited with making Indian classical music popular in the West, notably through his association with George Harrison of The Beatles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pandit Ravi Shankar won four Grammy Awards in his career, including for the Concert for Bangladesh (1971).

• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna (1999), India's highest civilian award, and also the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan.

• His daughters are the sitarist Anoushka Shankar and the singer Norah Jones.

NOTE

• Other Indian Grammy winners: Ustad Zakir Hussain (tabla), Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, A. R. Rahman (two Grammys for Slumdog Millionaire), Ricky Kej and Shankar Mahadevan (with Shakti, 2024).

question: The first battle of Tarain was fought between ________ .
option_1: Prithviraj Chauhan and Mohammad Bin Qasim
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The First Battle of Tarain (1191) was fought between Prithviraj Chauhan III (the Rajput ruler of Delhi–Ajmer) and Muhammad Ghori (Muizzuddin Muhammad bin Sam). Prithviraj Chauhan won and Ghori was defeated. (तराइन का प्रथम युद्ध — 1191)

• Tarain (Taraori) lies near Thanesar in present-day Haryana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Muhammad Ghori returned and defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, an event that laid the foundation of Muslim rule in northern India.

• Qutubuddin Aibak, Ghori's slave general, later founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.

NOTE

• Muhammad bin Qasim invaded Sindh in 712 CE (defeating Raja Dahir); Mahmud of Ghazni raided India 17 times between 1000 and 1027 CE, including the sack of the Somnath temple (1025) — neither fought at Tarain.

question: The process in which metals are extracted from their ores by heating beyond the melting point is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Smelting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Smelting" is the metallurgical process in which a metal is extracted from its ore by heating it beyond the melting point, usually with a reducing agent such as coke (carbon) and a flux (like limestone). (प्रगलन)

• Example: In a blast furnace, iron ore (haematite) is smelted with coke and limestone to obtain molten pig iron.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other metallurgical processes: Calcination (heating an ore in the absence/limited supply of air to remove moisture and volatile matter), Roasting (heating a sulphide ore strongly in the presence of air), Refining/Electrolysis (purifying the crude metal).

• "Flux" combines with impurities (gangue) to form slag, which is removed.

NOTE

• Option 1 "Spinning" relates to converting fibres into yarn (textiles), Option 3 "Heaving" means lifting/throwing with effort, and Option 4 "Extracting" is a general word, not the specific technical term asked for.

question: Which among the following vitamins influences iron absorption?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) greatly enhances the absorption of iron in the small intestine by reducing ferric iron (Fe³⁺) to the more absorbable ferrous form (Fe²⁺). (विटामिन C — लौह अवशोषण बढ़ाता है)

• This is why doctors advise taking iron tablets with lemon water or citrus juice, and why anaemia diets combine iron-rich foods with vitamin-C-rich foods.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Vitamin C is water-soluble; its deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, weakness). Sources: amla, guava, oranges, lemon, tomato, capsicum.

• Vitamin D aids calcium and phosphorus absorption (deficiency: rickets/osteomalacia); Vitamin K helps in blood clotting; Vitamin B12 is needed for red blood cell formation (deficiency: pernicious anaemia).

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C.

• Tea, coffee and calcium-rich foods inhibit iron absorption, whereas Vitamin C promotes it.

question: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Amendment Act, 2021 increases the upper limit for termination from 20 to ______ weeks for certain categories of women.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 raised the upper gestational limit for termination of pregnancy from 20 weeks to 24 weeks for special categories of women — such as survivors of rape, victims of incest, minors, differently-abled women and women whose marital status changes during pregnancy. (एमटीपी संशोधन अधिनियम 2021 — 24 सप्ताह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Under the amended Act, the opinion of one registered medical practitioner suffices up to 20 weeks, and of two practitioners for 20 to 24 weeks.

• Beyond 24 weeks, termination is allowed only in cases of substantial foetal abnormality, as diagnosed by a State-level Medical Board.

• The Act also protects the privacy of the woman — her identity cannot be revealed except to a person authorised by law.

NOTE

• The parent legislation is the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971. The 2021 amendment was passed to make abortion access safer and more inclusive, extending the benefit to unmarried women as well.

question: As of 2022, what is the capital of Maldives, a neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Male.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Male" is the capital and largest city of the Maldives, an island nation in the Indian Ocean and a maritime neighbour of India. (माले — मालदीव की राजधानी)

• The currency of the Maldives is the Maldivian Rufiyaa, and its official language is Dhivehi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Maldives is an archipelago of about 1,200 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls; it is the smallest Asian country by land area and population, and the lowest-lying country in the world.

• India and the Maldives share close ties; India's "Neighbourhood First" policy and the SAGAR vision (Security and Growth for All in the Region) cover the Maldives.

NOTE

• Option 1 Kavaratti is the capital of India's union territory Lakshadweep; Option 3 Colombo is the commercial capital of Sri Lanka (Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital); Option 4 Abu Dhabi is the capital of the UAE.

question: Renowned Rajasthani folk dancer Gulabo Sapera is recognized for ______ dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbeliya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gulabo Sapera is the world-renowned exponent of the Kalbeliya dance of Rajasthan, performed by women of the Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — राजस्थान)

• The dance imitates the movements of a serpent; dancers wear black swirling ghagharas (angrakhi) and move to the music of the been (pungi) and khanjari.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kalbeliya was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Gulabo Sapera was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2016.

• Other Rajasthani folk dances: Ghoomar, Kachhi Ghodi, Chari, Terah Taali, Bhavai.

NOTE

• Option 1 Bihu is the folk dance of Assam; Option 2 Garba belongs to Gujarat; Option 3 Jhumar/Jhumair is associated with Haryana, Punjab and the Chhotanagpur region.

question: Which God is worshipped during the festival of Chhath Puja?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhath Puja is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his sister/consort Chhathi Maiya (Usha). Devotees offer arghya (water offerings) to the setting and the rising sun while standing in a river or pond. (छठ पूजा — सूर्य देव)

• It is celebrated mainly in Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Nepal (Terai), on the sixth day (Shashthi) of the Kartika month.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The four-day rituals are: Nahay-Khay, Kharna (Lohanda), Sandhya Arghya (evening offering to the setting sun) and Usha Arghya (morning offering to the rising sun).

• It is one of the very few festivals in which the setting sun is worshipped, symbolising respect for decline as well as rise.

NOTE

• Other sun-related festivals and sites: Makar Sankranti, Pongal, the Konark Sun Temple (Odisha) and the Modhera Sun Temple (Gujarat).

question: Which acid is predominantly present in tomatoes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oxalic acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Oxalic acid is the acid predominantly associated with tomatoes (they also contain citric and malic acid). (टमाटर — ऑक्सैलिक अम्ल)

• Oxalic acid is also found in spinach, cabbage, beetroot and rhubarb; in large quantities it can bind calcium and contribute to kidney stones (calcium oxalate).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Common natural acids asked in SSC exams:

◦ Citric acid — lemon, orange, other citrus fruits

◦ Malic acid — apples

◦ Tartaric acid — tamarind, grapes

◦ Lactic acid — curd/milk products

◦ Acetic acid — vinegar

◦ Formic acid — ant sting, nettle

◦ Butyric acid — rancid butter

NOTE

• Carbonic acid (H₂CO₃) is formed when carbon dioxide dissolves in water — it is present in soft drinks/soda water, not tomatoes.

question: ________ is the father of the modern periodic table.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dmitri Mendeleev.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev is called the "father of the modern periodic table". In 1869 he arranged the known elements in order of increasing atomic mass and framed the Periodic Law: "The properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses." (दिमित्री मेंडलीफ)

• He boldly left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties — eka-aluminium (gallium), eka-boron (scandium) and eka-silicon (germanium) — all later confirmed.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Henry Moseley (1913) modified the law, showing that properties are a periodic function of the atomic number, giving us the modern periodic table (18 groups, 7 periods).

• John Newlands gave the Law of Octaves (1865); Dobereiner gave the Law of Triads (1817).

NOTE

• J. J. Thomson discovered the electron (1897) and gave the plum-pudding model; Ernest Rutherford discovered the nucleus (1911) through the gold-foil experiment and is called the father of nuclear physics.

question: Where is the deepest point on earth, the Mariana Trench, located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mariana Trench, the deepest known point on the Earth's surface, is located in the western Pacific Ocean, east of the Mariana Islands near Guam. (मारियाना ट्रेंच — प्रशांत महासागर)

• Its deepest point is the "Challenger Deep", about 10,994 metres (nearly 11 km) below sea level — deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The trench was formed by the subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath the Philippine Plate — a classic convergent plate boundary feature.

• The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean in the world; it is ringed by the "Ring of Fire", a belt of intense volcanic and earthquake activity.

NOTE

• Deepest points of other oceans: Puerto Rico Trench (Atlantic), Sunda/Java Trench (Indian Ocean), Molloy Deep (Arctic Ocean).

question: The Standard Meridian of India (82°30' E) passes through ______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's Standard Meridian is 82°30' E, which passes through Mirzapur (near Naini, Prayagraj) in Uttar Pradesh. Among the given options, it passes through Madhya Pradesh. (भारत की मानक याम्योत्तर — 82°30' पूर्व)

• Indian Standard Time (IST) is GMT/UTC + 5:30 hours, calculated from this meridian.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Standard Meridian passes through five states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

• India's longitudinal extent is 68°7' E to 97°25' E, and its latitudinal extent is 8°4' N to 37°6' N; the east–west time difference is about 2 hours, which is why a single standard meridian was adopted.

NOTE

• The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

question: Which famous Indian dancer is associated with Pandavani dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Teejan Bai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Teejan Bai is the most famous exponent of Pandavani, a folk ballad/narrative performing art of Chhattisgarh in which episodes from the Mahabharata (especially the story of the Pandavas and Bhima) are sung and enacted. (पंडवानी — तीजन बाई)

• She performs in the Kapalik style, holding a tambura decorated with ghungroos as a prop.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Teejan Bai has been honoured with the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2003), Padma Vibhushan (2019) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• Pandavani has two styles: Vedamati (seated, sober) and Kapalik (standing, dramatic).

NOTE

• Option 1 Vyjayanthimala — Bharatanatyam; Option 2 Pandit Birju Maharaj — Kathak (Lucknow gharana); Option 3 Vempati Chinna Satyam — Kuchipudi.

question: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is March 23, 1931.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru were hanged in Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931 in connection with the Lahore Conspiracy Case (the killing of the police officer J. P. Saunders in December 1928). (23 मार्च 1931 — शहीद दिवस)

• 23 March is observed in India as "Shaheed Diwas / Martyrs' Day".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Saunders was shot in revenge for the death of Lala Lajpat Rai, who died after a lathi charge during the protest against the Simon Commission (1928).

• On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw non-lethal bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly, shouting "Inquilab Zindabad", and courted arrest to "make the deaf hear".

• Bhagat Singh wrote the famous essay "Why I am an Atheist" in jail.

NOTE

• They belonged to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), reorganised in 1928 under Chandra Shekhar Azad.

• 30 January (Gandhiji's death anniversary) is also observed as Martyrs' Day.

question: Rangarajan Committee is associated with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Estimation of poverty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rangarajan Committee, headed by Dr. C. Rangarajan (former RBI Governor and Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the PM), was constituted in 2012 and submitted its report in 2014 on the methodology for the estimation of poverty in India. (गरीबी आकलन समिति)

• It raised the poverty line fixed by the Tendulkar Committee to about ₹32 per day in rural areas and ₹47 per day in urban areas (2011-12 prices), estimating 29.5% of the population as poor in 2011-12.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Earlier poverty-estimation committees: Lakdawala Committee (1993), Tendulkar Committee (2009) — Tendulkar had estimated poverty at 21.9% in 2011-12.

• Poverty estimates in India were traditionally based on NSSO consumption expenditure surveys; the NITI Aayog now also publishes a Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).

NOTE

• Other Rangarajan-headed panels dealt with gas pricing and the disinvestment of PSUs; but the committee most associated with him in SSC exams is the one on poverty estimation.

question: In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi successfully led a strike of __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mill workers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi led the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, supporting the cotton mill workers of Ahmedabad in their demand for a wage increase (a 35% "plague bonus"). (अहमदाबाद मिल हड़ताल — 1918)

• Gandhiji undertook his first hunger strike (fast unto death) in India on this occasion to keep the workers united and non-violent; the dispute was settled through arbitration and the workers got a 35% wage rise.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1917 — Champaran Satyagraha (Bihar): Gandhiji's first satyagraha in India, for indigo cultivators oppressed by the tinkathia system.

• 1918 — Kheda Satyagraha (Gujarat): for peasants who could not pay land revenue after crop failure; Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel emerged as a leader here.

• The Majoor Mahajan Sangh (Textile Labour Association) of Ahmedabad grew out of this movement.

NOTE

• Sequence to remember: Champaran (1917) → Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) → Kheda (1918) — Gandhiji's first three satyagrahas in India, all before the Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919.

question: The famous Dhamek Stupa is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Dhamek Stupa is located at Sarnath, near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. It marks the spot where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon to his five disciples after attaining enlightenment — the event known as Dharmachakra Pravartana ("turning of the wheel of law"). (धमेख स्तूप — सारनाथ, उत्तर प्रदेश)

• The present massive cylindrical structure was built around 500 CE (Gupta period), replacing an earlier structure commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in about 249 BCE.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Also at Sarnath is the Ashoka Pillar with the Lion Capital, adopted as India's State Emblem in 1950; the Dharma Chakra from its abacus appears on the national flag.

• The four great Buddhist sites: Lumbini (birth, Nepal), Bodh Gaya (enlightenment, Bihar), Sarnath (first sermon, UP) and Kushinagar (mahaparinirvana, UP).

NOTE

• The Sanchi Stupa is in Madhya Pradesh (a UNESCO World Heritage Site, built by Ashoka); the Amaravati Stupa is in Andhra Pradesh.

question: The Legislative Council of a State comprises not more than ________ of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of the State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is one-third.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 171 of the Constitution, the total strength of a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) shall not exceed one-third of the total membership of the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) of that State, and in no case shall it be less than 40. (विधान परिषद — विधानसभा की सदस्य संख्या का अधिकतम एक-तिहाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Composition of a Legislative Council (Article 171): about 1/3 elected by MLAs, 1/3 by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, and the remaining 1/6 nominated by the Governor from persons with special knowledge in literature, science, art, cooperative movement and social service.

• The Council is a permanent house (it cannot be dissolved); one-third of its members retire every two years, and the term of a member is 6 years.

• Under Article 169, Parliament may create or abolish a Legislative Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority.

NOTE

• States with a Legislative Council include Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. The Council is a weaker second chamber — it can only delay ordinary bills for a limited period and has no effective say over money bills.

question: Meri Policy Mere Hath scheme was launched by ______ Ministry of India in 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Meri Policy Mere Hath" was launched in 2022 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare as a doorstep distribution drive of crop insurance policy documents under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). (मेरी पॉलिसी मेरे हाथ — कृषि एवं किसान कल्याण मंत्रालय)

• Its aim is to ensure that every insured farmer physically holds his/her policy document and knows the details of the coverage, the claim process, land records and the grievance-redressal mechanism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The PMFBY was launched in 2016; farmers pay a premium of 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops, and the rest is shared by the Centre and the States.

• Other schemes of this Ministry: PM-KISAN, Kisan Credit Card (KCC), e-NAM, PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana, Soil Health Card.

NOTE

• The campaign was rolled out along with the "Kisan Bhagidari, Prathmikta Hamari" campaign of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

question: In the situation of liquidity trap, the speculative money demand function becomes ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is infinitely elastic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a "liquidity trap", the rate of interest is so low that everyone expects it to rise (and bond prices to fall), so people are willing to hold any amount of money rather than bonds. Hence the speculative demand for money becomes perfectly (infinitely) elastic with respect to the interest rate. (तरलता जाल — मुद्रा की सट्टा माँग पूर्णतः लोचदार)

• Graphically, the liquidity preference (money demand) curve becomes horizontal at that very low rate of interest.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The concept comes from J. M. Keynes, who identified three motives for holding money: the transaction motive, the precautionary motive and the speculative motive.

• In a liquidity trap, monetary policy becomes ineffective — increasing the money supply cannot push interest rates down further, so Keynes advocated fiscal policy (government spending) to revive demand.

NOTE

• Japan's economy in the 1990s and several economies after the 2008 global financial crisis are cited as real-world examples of a liquidity trap.

• Related idea: elasticity here measures the responsiveness of money demand to a change in the interest rate; "infinitely elastic" = perfectly elastic (a horizontal curve).

question: The Rampurva bull that was part of a Mauryan pillar found in Rampurwa, Bihar is now been placed at __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtrapati Bhavan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rampurva Bull capital, a beautifully polished Mauryan sandstone bull that once crowned an Ashokan pillar at Rampurwa in West Champaran district, Bihar, is now displayed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi. (रामपुरवा वृषभ — राष्ट्रपति भवन)

• It stands in the Durbar Hall/entrance area of Rashtrapati Bhavan and is celebrated for the characteristic Mauryan polish (chamak).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rampurva site yielded two Ashokan pillars — one with a bull capital and one with a lion capital; the lion capital is in the Indian Museum, Kolkata.

• Ashokan pillars are made of Chunar sandstone, are monolithic, and carry Brahmi inscriptions of Ashoka's edicts.

NOTE

• The most famous Mauryan capital is the Lion Capital of Sarnath, adopted as India's State Emblem. Other well-known capitals include the Rampurva Bull, the Sankissa Elephant and the Lauriya Nandangarh Lion.

question: Which country will host the Men's Cricket World Cup in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 (the 13th edition) was hosted by India from 5 October to 19 November 2023 — the first time a single country hosted the entire tournament. (भारत — पुरुष क्रिकेट विश्व कप 2023 का मेज़बान)

• The final was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, where Australia beat India by 6 wickets to win their sixth title.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Virat Kohli was the Player of the Tournament with a record 765 runs, including his 50th ODI century; Mohammed Shami took 24 wickets.

• India had earlier co-hosted the World Cup in 1987, 1996 and 2011, and won the title in 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (M. S. Dhoni).

NOTE

• The ICC (International Cricket Council) has its headquarters in Dubai, UAE. The ODI World Cup is held every four years.

question: In which country was the ICC Cricket World Cup (Women's) 2022, held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Zealand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Women's Cricket World Cup 2022 (the 12th edition) was hosted by New Zealand from 4 March to 3 April 2022. (न्यूज़ीलैंड — महिला क्रिकेट विश्व कप 2022)

• Australia won the title, beating England by 71 runs in the final at Hagley Oval, Christchurch — their seventh Women's World Cup crown.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Alyssa Healy (Australia) scored a record 170 runs in the final and was named Player of the Match as well as Player of the Tournament.

• India, led by Mithali Raj, failed to qualify for the semi-finals; this was Mithali Raj's last World Cup before her retirement.

NOTE

• India has been runner-up in the Women's World Cup twice — in 2005 (South Africa) and 2017 (England). Australia is the most successful team in the competition.
